text:
ana: Heads-up — onboarding llama-3-8k variant. We see a perf cliff past 2k tokens, and kernel selection falls back to generic matmul for attention. Suspect HF config missing rope_scaling and n_heads doesn't match state_dict.

mike: Can you paste the profiler snippet?

ana: profiler snippet:```
Kernel chosen: generic_matmul
attention: latency 12.3ms -> 39.8ms after 2k tokens
KV cache writes/sec: 0.8 -> 2.9 (increased due to full-copy fallback)
Fallback reason: qkv reshape mismatch (expected (batch, heads, seq, head_dim))
```

ana: HF config we got from hf:```
{"hidden_size": 4096, "intermediate_size": 11008, "num_attention_heads": 32}
```  <-- no rope_scaling, no rotary dims declared so runtime guesses head_dim=128 which is wrong.

julia: Oof. If state dict has q,k,v shaped for 40 heads (or fused layout) we will mis-detect and pick slow path. Any safetensors metadata?

ana: safetensors header shows: `metadata": {"model_variant":"llama-3-8k","heads":40}` but HF config disagrees. Looks like conversion script dropped metadata into safetensors but didn't align hf_config.json.

ken: Quick mitigation: runtime should infer head_count/head_dim from weight shapes before relying on hf_config. We already have weight-shape inspection for linear layers, just need to apply to q/k/v fused params. I'll send a PR.

mike: Also batching heuristics: once kernel falls back we get per-request serialization because our continuous batching expects fast matmul GPU kernel. We should add a sanity check to disable large batching when fallback triggers. Add a switch: `runtime.disable_batching_on_fallback=true`.

julia: For immediate hack, can we add a CI model-sanity test that: 1) loads safetensors and hf_config; 2) checks head_count parity; 3) runs a 2k token generation smoke perf (1 request) and asserts kernel != generic_matmul? If it fails, block release.

ci-bot: I ran quick check on the CI image: `python -c "from safetensors import safe_open; print(safe_open('model.safetensors').metadata)"` -> returned heads=40. HF config still shows 32.

ana: Proposed next steps: 1) ken PR to infer qkv shapes and set kernel flags (owner: ken) 2) mike add runtime flag to reduce batching when fallback (owner: mike) 3) julia add CI sanity test + conversion script check (owner: julia) 4) ops re-convert the model artifact to sync hf_config (owner: infra).

ken: I'll include a small helper `detect_attention_layout(tensors)` that inspects `.shape` for q,k,v and fused qkv patterns and returns (heads, head_dim, fused). If mismatch with hf_config, log error and prefer weights.

mike: I'll also add telemetry metric `runtime.attention.layout_mismatch` to catch other models.

julia: Can someone paste the conversion command that created this artifact? we need to fix it upstream.

ana: conversion call used by infra: `python tools/convert_to_safetensors.py --from hf --model hf/llama-3-8k --out model.safetensors --embed-rotary True` (looks like a manual flag mismatch).

mike: TL;DR: root cause = HF config drift vs safetensors metadata -> runtime mis-detects qkv dims -> kernel fallback -> big perf regression + KV cache behavior change. Fixes: weight-shape inference, CI sanity, conversion script validation, and a short-term runtime flag to limit batching. :eyes:

ana: I'll open a tracking ticket and link PRs. Thanks all :thumbsup:
